name: Flex Conveyor

points.label: Path points
points.desc: The bed runs from its infeed (the part origin, heading +X) along a smooth curve through these points, part-local metres, the last one being the discharge end. Drag the dots in the viewport to pull it into shape: S-curves, a turn through a door, a loop. The length follows.

length.label: Length (m)
length.desc: The bed length along its sections, written by the path drag: it sets how far each section is stretched.

infeedBrakes.label: Infeed brakes
infeedBrakes.desc: The caster brakes under the infeed end are on. Walking, a braked end cannot be pulled, and pulling the other end further than the bed reaches stops there instead of rolling the unit after you. The editor places it wherever you drag it.

dischargeBrakes.label: Discharge brakes
dischargeBrakes.desc: The caster brakes under the discharge end are on. Walking, a braked end cannot be pulled, and pulling the other end further than the bed reaches stops there instead of rolling the unit after you. The editor places it wherever you drag it.

width.label: Width (m)
width.desc: Roller width between the scissor sides.

sideGuides.label: Side guides
sideGuides.desc: Low rails along both edges that keep product on the bed through a tight bend. Off, as a flex usually ships: a gentle bed carries without them, and a hard bend or a U-turn wants them on.

standHeight.label: Stand height (m)
standHeight.desc: Height of the roller tops above the floor. The legs under every hinge reach down to their casters.

fpmUnits.label: PLC speed in FPM
fpmUnits.desc: The unit the PLC commands this conveyor in. On: feet per minute. Off: metres per second. The speed tag is a REAL either way, so switching changes what its value means and never how the program declares it. Set by the scene Units (Scene Properties), which switch every conveyor together, so the Inspector does not show it. A conveyor saved before this switch existed is in metres per second.

speedFpm.label: Speed
speedFpm.desc: Surface speed in feet per minute. Negative runs it backwards. A program can command this through the FPM speed tag below.

speed.label: Speed
speed.desc: Surface speed along the bed. Negative runs it back toward the infeed.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Connect this part to a PLC program. Its tags appear once this is on.

speedTag.label: Speed tag (m/s)
speedTag.desc: The program commands the bed speed here, replacing the Speed field above. Once bound it takes over even if no program drives it, and an undriven tag reads 0.

speedFpmTag.label: Speed tag (FPM)
speedFpmTag.desc: The program commands surface speed here in feet per minute, replacing the Speed field above, which then shows the live value read-only. Once BOUND this takes over even if no program writes it, so an unwritten tag holds the conveyor at 0.

runTag.label: Run tag (rollers run while true)
runTag.desc: Start/stop gate: while a program drives this tag false the bed stands still, and true it runs at its speed. Until a program actually drives it the bed runs, so a merely-typed tag does not stop it.

accumulate.label: Zone accumulation
accumulate.desc: Zero-pressure accumulation: each section is a zone with its own photo-eye, and a zone holding a case stops while the zone ahead is full, so product queues with gaps and never pushes. Off, the whole bed runs as one. Sections must be longer than the product.

releaseTag.label: Release tag (discharge zone runs while true)
releaseTag.desc: With accumulation on: the discharge zone lets its case go only while a program drives this true, so the line takes product when it wants it. Unbound, or not driven by a program, the discharge zone always releases.

meterGap.label: Release spacing (s)
meterGap.desc: With accumulation on: the least time between two cases leaving the discharge end. A queue released all at once goes out a zone apart; this meters it wider, to the spacing the line downstream is set up for.

fullTag.label: Full tag (first zone eye covered)
fullTag.desc: True while the first zone eye is covered: the last case has not cleared it, or the queue has backed up to it. Put the next case down (a case length and a gap behind that eye) only while this is false, and cases can never land on each other.

showBeam.label: Show beams
showBeam.desc: Draw each zone photo-eye beam across the bed: green where the zone is clear, red from the eye to the case it sees.
